newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS-Santander takes over Mexico's Invermexico.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Santander takes over Mexico's Invermexico.

text.p: Spanish bank Banco Santander SA will take over Mexico's Grupo Financiero Invermexico SA next year in return for a huge capital injection that will save Invermexico's troubled bank unit Banco Mexicano, banking authorities said on Thursday.

Santander becomes only the second foreign bank to buy a majority stake in a Mexican financial group following the 1995 purchase of Probursa financial group by fellow Spanish bank Banco Bilbao Vizcaya.

Invermexico will raise $425 million in new capital to shore up Banco Mexicano, Mexico's fourth largest bank with some $11 billion in assets, the Banking and Securities Commission (CNBV) said in a statement.

Santander, Spain's largest bank, will provide the bulk of the new capital, about $378 million, while Invermexico will raise the remaining $47 million from its own shareholders. Santander's stake in the group should end up at about 75 percent, analysts said.

Mexican law was changed in 1995 at the height of the peso crisis to allow foreign banks to buy majority stakes in their Mexican counterparts in exchange for cleaning up their balance sheets, which were hammered by soaring interest rates that followed the peso crash.

Santander has done corporate banking in Mexico during the past few years but will face a tough task competing head-to-head against Mexican heavyweights Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival and Grupo Financiero Bancomer.
"It's a good time to buy a Mexican bank, although expanding into retail banking into someone else's territory is risky business," said Alberto Sanchez, a bank analyst at Bear Stearns in New York.
Santander will use its experience in Chile, where it successfully entered the retail market through its purchase this year of Banco Osorno, to help in cracking Mexico's market, Sanchez said.
Mexican finance minister Guillermo Ortiz said the move should help competition in the banking system and will mean better borrowing conditions for Mexican consumers and businesses.

As part of the deal, Banco Mexicano will sell an additional $2.364 billion in portfolio to the government's FOBAPROA bank support fund. It had already sold about 7.3 billion pesos in past-due loans to the government, according to analysts.
For its part, Santander will create reserve provisions at Invermexico equal to 100 percent of current capital at Banco Mexicano, the commission said.
Grupo Financiero Invermexico's President Carlos Gomez y Gomez will continue as head of the financial group, Santander said.
